points.description: States that a·b is positive only when a and b are both positive or both negative (both nonzero with the same sign). Equivalent wording earns the mark.

Finds the probability for each same-sign case using interval lengths: a > 0 has probability 1/4 (length 1 out of 4) and b > 0 has probability 2/3 (length 4 out of 6), giving 1/6 for both positive; a < 0 has probability 3/4 and b < 0 has probability 1/3 (length 2 out of 6), giving 1/4 for both negative. Equivalent correct fractions or area-based methods earn the marks.
points.partial_credit: 0.2 for a correct case probability (1/6 for both positive or 1/4 for both negative), with the other case correct or not, provided the method is valid. Full 0.4 requires both case probabilities correct.

points.description: Adds the two case probabilities correctly to obtain 5/12 and gives this as the final answer as a common fraction.
